title: Security posture discovery - Pioneer Health
summary: Intro call to map Pioneer Health security requirements for evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Main topics: SOC 2 / ISO requirements, SSO (SAML/SCIM), RBAC, audit logging and retention, encryption / KMS (customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed), VPC / on-prem network patterns, data retention and deletion, and next steps to share docs and schedule a technical deep-dive and pilot.

Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
On-prem / VPC networking and private control plane

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-05-07 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Ethan Wong (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Pioneer Head of Security), Marc Rivera (CTO), Anita Gomez (DevOps), Daniel Park (SRE)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for making time, appreciate it. this is just a quick security posture discovery to understand Pioneer Health's controls and constraints.
[00:08] Laura Chen: thanks Jordan. we wanted to run through SOC2, iso stuff, and the SSO requirements primarily. we evaluate hosted providers but we have some regulated data flows so dedicated or private may be required.
[00:18] Marc Rivera: yup; timeline wise we're aiming for a pilot in q3, procurement later. security is the gating factor.
[00:25] Maya Patel: great. quick intro from me — i'm the SE focused on infra and security integrations. we typically pair AE + SE on these. i'll ask a few infra-y questions and then we can follow with deeper tech dive if helpful.
[00:36] Anita Gomez: cool. on our side we run EHR ingestion pipelines, PHI redaction happens upstream, but the inference outputs may still be considered regulated depending on downstream use. so we need clarity on data residency and retention.
[00:49] Ethan Wong: understood. first question — do you have an internal requirement for SOC 2 Type II and/or ISO27001?
[00:56] Laura Chen: SOC2 Type II is required for any hosted vendor. ISO27001 is preferred but not mandatory. we also will need SAML SSO and SCIM, and audit logs with at least 1 year retention, ideally 7 years for investigatory purposes.
[01:12] Maya Patel: noted. to confirm Redwood — for our hosted API we are SOC 2 Type II compliant and have ISO27001 attestation as well, we can share the reports. we support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning for enterprise accounts and offer RBAC with fine-grained roles.
[01:30] Marc Rivera: is the audit log tamper-evident? how are logs stored, and can we export them to our SIEM?
[01:38] Jordan Lee: good q. logs are stored in an immutable store and we provide streaming export to common SIEMs and S3. retention configurable per account — default 1 year, can be extended. we also provide redwood-managed archive and support push to customer's cloud.
[01:52] Daniel Park: what about encryption and KMS? we need customer-managed keys for some workloads.
[01:58] Maya Patel: we support CMEK for Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted supports Redwood-managed keys by default and customer-managed keys via an enterprise plan — we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM-backed providers. for private deployment the customer controls keys fully in their KMS. note — there's an operational runbook for key rotation and split-key scenarios.
[02:20] Anita Gomez: how about data in transit — TLS mutual?
[02:23] Ethan Wong: all API traffic is TLS 1.2+; mutual TLS is supported for Private and Dedicated in restricted network setups. hosted can support mTLS via customer request on enterprise tier.
[02:34] Laura Chen: if we do hosted with Redwood-managed keys, can we restrict redwood support access to logs and data? we need least privilege and proof of separation.
[02:43] Jordan Lee: yes. RBAC controls limit staff access, and access is logged — support access is gated via Just-In-Time access and requires an approval workflow. we can provide auditor access patterns and a redacted demo of the access logs.
[02:55] Marc Rivera: what's the difference operationally between Dedicated and Private from a security standpoint?
[03:00] Maya Patel: key diffs: Dedicated = isolated GPU pools and network tenancy within Redwood's control plane, but we manage the control plane. it gives capacity isolation and dedicated tenancy for workloads. Private = customer-managed control plane with optional on-prem package or VPC-hosted control plane, keys and audit logs live in your environment if desired. Private has the highest surface for compliance because you control the network and key material.
[03:26] Laura Chen: about network — we want VPC peering and egress control. can you do private endpoints?
[03:31] Maya Patel: yes, we can do private endpoints and VPC peering for Dedicated; Private provides customer-managed VPCs and optional on-prem. egress rules and IP allowlists supported.
[03:42] Anita Gomez: on audit logs — can we set retention and legal hold? also need info on PII deletion and data retention policies for prompt logs and KV cache.
[03:51] Ethan Wong: audit retention is configurable, and we support legal hold by flagging records to prevent deletion. for prompt logs we offer configurable retention and can purge or redact data on request. Kv cache terminology sometimes appears as K-V cash in transcriptions — our KV cache is ephemeral and used for performance; persistent storage of prompts/outputs depends on config and is not stored for hosted default unless you opt-in for logs.
[04:13] Laura Chen: okay so for PHI we likely want Private or Dedicated with CMEK and audit export to our SIEM, plus SSO/SCIM integration.
[04:21] Marc Rivera: also interested in SAML: does Redwood support Azure AD and Okta?
[04:25] Jordan Lee: yes both Okta and Azure AD are supported; SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning supported out of box.
[04:31] Daniel Park: any external pen-test reports and vulnerability scanning cadence?
[04:35] Maya Patel: Redwood does quarterly vulnerability scans and annual third-party pen tests. we can share the executive summary of the pentest and code-level guidance for self-assessment.
[04:47] Anita Gomez: what about data residency — are there region options?
[04:50] Jordan Lee: hosted has region selection across NA and EU, and soon APAC; Dedicated can be provisioned in chosen regions and Private lets you control the region fully. region-based data residency policies available for enterprise.
[04:59] Laura Chen: any integrations for KMS logs or key usage audit? we need to show key usage to auditors.
[05:05] Ethan Wong: yes, we can surface KMS audit events in the exported logs if you use customer-managed keys and forward to your SIEM.
[05:11] Marc Rivera: for the pilot — can we do a small benchmark on some of our workloads? latency and cost per token matter.
[05:17] Maya Patel: absolutely. plan would be: we run a 1-week benchmark on Dedicated and compare to hosted with same model variants; we'll instrument latency, token cost, failure rates. we'll need sample prompts and representative payloads plus network access to run tests if you choose Dedicated/Private.
[05:34] Laura Chen: procurement — what's the contract minimum for Dedicated or Private?
[05:37] Jordan Lee: Dedicated typically has a 6-12 month reserved capacity commit; Private is custom licensed with enterprise terms. we'll share a draft term sheet.
[05:46] Marc Rivera: ok — last question: are there any known compliance gaps vs healthcare regs like HIPAA?
[05:52] Maya Patel: Redwood can support HIPAA-covered workloads under a Business Associate Agreement; we have controls in place but signing an appropriate BAA and choosing Private/Dedicated with CMEK is the recommended path for maximal compliance. we can share our BAA template.
[06:05] Jordan Lee: great, i'll send SOC2, ISO docs, BAA template, and a link to our security page. we'll also get a tech deep-dive scheduled — Maya you'll lead that?
[06:12] Maya Patel: yep i'll follow up with times.
[06:15] Laura Chen: thanks everyone. we'll compile the questionnaire and send it over.
[06:18] Jordan Lee: perfect. recap: share docs, schedule deep dive and benchmark, Pioneer sends questionnaire and network diagram. thanks all.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had minor errors (KV vs K-V cash, some proper nouns). speaker overlaps occasionally labeled as same speaker.
notes: Call ended with clear next steps to exchange SOC2/ISO docs and schedule technical deep dive; Pioneer leaning toward Dedicated/Private due to PHI requirements.
